ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: The visible fluke surface is characterized by a high ratio of low-intensity (black) to high-intensity (white) pixels, with dark pigmentation covering approximately 98% of the observable area.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: The surface is a contiguous solid black region. High-contrast, high-intensity pixel clusters are restricted to the extreme distal tips of both the left and right lobes at the lateral margins.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Visible shallow V-shaped notch at the center with an obtuse angle of approximately 140 degrees and a shallow pixel-depth depression.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Trailing edges exhibit low-frequency, low-amplitude irregularities along the primary spans, transitioning to high-amplitude, irregular jagged clusters at the distal lobe tips.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: The leading edges follow a straight, upward-sloping trajectory; the trailing edges display a mild concave curvature as they converge toward the median notch.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dense, roughly circular high-contrast pixel clusters (white/grey) are localized at the outer tips of both lobes, suggesting barnacle attachments or scarring.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: The distal tips of both lobes show irregular, non-linear physical margins, indicative of localized tissue erosion or heavy colonization by sessile organisms.
other_distinctive_markers: The pigmentation is exceptionally uniform across the entire visible ventral surface, creating a silhouette effect with minimal internal pixel variance.
